messages:
olivia_support: Heads-up — customer acme-ads opened a ticket: embedding requests getting 403 'invalid_api_key' even though they haven't rotated keys. They pasted a curl and server response.

olivia_support: curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input": "test"}'

olivia_support: Response body: {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_api_key"}}

devin_infra: can you paste the request_id / response headers from the request? looks like a 403 not a 401 so might be entitlement gating.

olivia_support: request-id: req_01HXYZ1234, response-headers: x-plan-check: failed, x-plan-reason: quota_exceeded, x-server: auth-service-2.1

entitlement-bot: plan_check: tenant=acme-ads result=DENY reason=seat_quota_exceeded sku=team_pro timestamp=2026-03-15T18:22:40Z

marco_backend: @olivia_support @devin_infra this matches a known mapping bug: when plan check fails we currently return 403 with body code 'invalid_api_key' in auth-service. The plan gating path wraps the error into a generic auth error for historical SDK compatibility.

marco_backend: repro I ran: POST /v1/embeddings with tenant header set to acme-ads and with a valid key -> auth-service returned 403 + code invalid_api_key. If tenant plan is updated the same key succeeds.

sara_csm: I spoke to billing: customer had pending invoice and was on a trial-to-paid transition; payment pending + seat limit hit. They upgraded the seats an hour ago.

olivia_support: Customer says after upgrade they retried and calls succeeded. They asked why the UI showed 'invalid key' which made them think they needed to rotate. They almost revoked their key.

devin_infra: Not ideal. Two action items: 1) immediate: update observability so support can surface x-plan-reason in the support UI; 2) medium-term: change the error body so plan-denied returns code 'plan_entitlement' and message 'plan does not permit this usage' instead of invalid_api_key. That way SDKs can differentiate.

marco_backend: I'll open a small PR to change the error code and add a migration flag gated by an env var so we can canary it (auth-service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/487). It will also emit metric auth.plan_denied.{reason}.

sara_csm: Also will send a note to the customer explaining the root cause and that their key was never compromised.

olivia_support: Quick patch deployed to canary. Devin, can you add a dashboard panel pulling x-plan-reason and the new metric?

devin_infra: yes, will add panels and an alert when plan_denied spikes for a tenant.

marco_backend: tested canary on staging, behavior looks correct: 403 with body {"error":{"message":"Plan entitlement blocked","code":"plan_entitlement"}} and x-plan-reason header preserved.

olivia_support: Customer confirmed resolution after billing update. They were told not to rotate keys and to retry. Closing the ticket once PR deploys to prod. :tada:

sara_csm: capturing this in runbook under support -> entitlement-gates so next time support can quickly check x-plan-reason and call out billing before recommending key rotation.

marco_backend: follow-up: will also add a note in the SDK error mapping docs so front-end devs don't treat 403+invalid_api_key as immediate key rotation.

olivia_support: thanks team — closing thread after prod deploy.
